source.cleaned_file: goldbound/014 - I Finally Unlocked WESTFALL, Time To Farm! - Goldbound Episode 14.en-orig.txt
source.quote: And all right, now let's get back to farming in Westfall. And this zone has a special place in my heart. Nothing beats Alliance questing nostalgia. It's hard to top and I'm sure we'll uncover some great stories and items along the way. Now, speaking of quests, we've had a few quests from our days in Elwin that sent us here, which we can finally actually hand in and complete. But we do want to be careful with the zone because we don't want to finish quests too early because after Cataclysm, completing quest lines tends to change what mobs you have available. So, we'll have to look out for that. But let's get a first overview of the zone and check out its borders, unlock any paths to any new zones for the randomizer. Well, not exactly. And to be 100% honest with you, when I was checking out the southern edge of the map where the river leads into Stranglethorn, I thought maybe this would be a walkable path and potentially put Stranglethorn on the randomizer. But unexpectedly, the stretch just east of the tower, still on the westfall side of the river, is actually technically flagged as Duskwood. So, Goldilock ended up making his first misstep into a locked zone, unintentionally discovering the border of Duskwood. And sure, arguably, this is just some poor border design, but a misstep all the same. And the rules are the rules. So stay tuned because I have a forfeit lined up that'll make Goldie pay a little bit of a price for this. But before we get into that, there's one thing I've been dying to do. Dead mines. So let's head there.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/014 - I Finally Unlocked WESTFALL, Time To Farm! - Goldbound Episode 14.en-orig.txt
source.quote: And while we're heading over, I have noticed, and you might as well, that there's a few things in Westfall and eventually Dead Mines that are a little different from the classic versions. And a lot has changed here after the Cataclysm. Landmarks, quests, mobs, and even the dungeon itself. So, for context, the Dead Mines has always been rich in lore, and there's plenty of lore that actually predates what I'm going to talk about, but back in classic World of Warcraft, it was overrun and the layer of the Defias Brotherhood, led by Edwin Van Clee. And back in classic, he was the final boss of the dungeon. And players sent by Brian Stoutmantle to put an end to the Defias would ultimately slay Van Clee and return with proof of his head. So, if you played classic, you may have been one of those adventurers who delivered the killing blow. So, in the lore, Edwin Van Clee was actually killed during that quest line. And fast forward to Cataclysm, when a lot of the zone and dungeon changed, it was discovered that that assassination that me and baby you parttook in was actually witnessed by someone, his daughter, Vanessa Van Clee. This is where it gets kind of crazy because in the silence after Van Cleiff's fall, Vanessa rebuilt the Brotherhood with new soldiers and new henchmen and took up his plans to assault Stormwind once again. So that's where Deadmines lands right now in current WoW. The final boss being Vanessa Van Clee, which is just a brief overview, but it explains why the dungeon looks and feels a little different now compared to back in the day. So what does this mean for gold farming and dead mines? Well, quite a bit. So, the Cataclysm version of Dead Mines actually has a new loot table, which means some of the old school transmog that could be farmed here, doesn't actually exist anymore, and there's some new pieces that are cataclysm based. But the big question I'm wondering, mostly for Goldie's own zone look, what about the classic rogue items, the Defas set? Well, sadly, the full set no longer drops here. The defied overseers still dropped the gloves and the leggings at a 1.18% drop chance with the boots, belt, and armor still unavailable and not on their loot tables. Our goalies dreams of walking around in Defia garb gone forever? Well, maybe not entirely. So, on our first run through Deadmines, we actually managed to grab a red Defas mask, which gives us a decent mirror of the look. And we also got a few of the iconic rogue weapons.

source.quote: Cruel Barb and Buzzer Blade. They're soulbound, so we can't sell them, but they perfectly fit our look right now as zone transbox. But while we're farming away on deadlines, what else can drop here that we might actually be able to sell to other players? Well, there's still some solid blue items worth chasing. The Defas Rapier. This drops from Defas Watchmen and Pirates, which does have a cool appearance, but it's only worth about 1 to 2,000 gold, although it isn't even the lowest drop rate, so you might be able to get a few of these. There's also the Goblin Screwdriver. Another weapon worth about 1 to 2,000 gold. Again, nothing too crazy, but always a good staple to add to the transmog shelves. And there's also Goblin Male Leggings. This one only drops from the goblin ship builders near the end of the dungeon, but has a market value of about 2 to 3,000 gold. And across the dungeon, there's some usual green BOE's, pieces of the cadet and journeyman sets, but most of the coolest boss loot is binded on pickup. And since we're running through Chromy time, loot tables can be a little odd. So, I'll have to log a few more runs to really nail down what's dropping and check back with you. But there is one other notable drop. The green wing macaw. This is a battle pet that can be obtained at the end of the dungeon. Now, on the surface, this seems like just a vendor pet worth about 200 gold. But travelers, it's actually a window into something bigger. A secret quest line. one that can only be done by an outlaw rogue. And last I checked, we fit the bill. So, here's how it works.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/014 - I Finally Unlocked WESTFALL, Time To Farm! - Goldbound Episode 14.en-orig.txt
source.quote: I mentioned earlier that some of the mobs in Westfall actually change after completing a few quests. Now, I'm not 100% sure on all of them, but I do know of a couple and I want to test them first. So, around Sentinel Hill, you'll find plenty of nles similar to the vibe in Red Ridge. But after finishing the story quests, many of these NLES get replaced with Defas mobs. Now, the new Defas mobs have their own loot worth farming. But before that, let's take a closer look at the nles. And the noles attacking Sentinel Hill are actually hyper spawns. That means they can be killed frequently and fast. Now, unfortunately, their loot tables don't include any big ticket items. It's mostly midvalue greens and whites from the zone tables, but the angle here really is linen cloth. And back in the day, I know that these nules were the most efficient linen cloth farm in the game. Not so much for a solo rogue. If you had a fiveman group positioned properly, you could hyperspawn kill these insanely fast. And the cloth yield was off the charts for us. We can only hold one side of the front line here and keep a mini hyperspawn rolling. But still, there's about four or five nles that we can kill repeatedly. So, it's time to update the target macro with a new pistol shot to farm it efficiently.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/014 - I Finally Unlocked WESTFALL, Time To Farm! - Goldbound Episode 14.en-orig.txt
source.quote: And this one little vendor unlocks a massive world of potential tailoring and enchanting shuffles. And that means finding a reliable linen cloth farm actually has merit again. So, we can't just give up with the noles around Sentinel Hill. And I know that there's some more nles to the north. They're not exactly hypers spawn nles because they're spread out so far, but they have very similar loot tables and a lot of the same archetypes. And after doing some preliminary testing, we're actually getting the normal amount of linen cloth that we should have been from the other nles. However, this isn't a fairy tale farm because 3 to 4 minutes in, we stopped getting drops and we stopped getting cloth. And I don't know if I could even call this an open world loot bug anymore. I'm going to start calling it the anti-hyperspawn mechanic because at this point I'm pretty sure Blizzard either knows it's there or intentionally put it in. Which, if we're going to be honest, isn't too bad for us cuz it does prevent fiveman groups from farming trade goods endlessly and tanking the value of these low-level items. But it does mean we need to get a little more creative. So travelers, where does the anti-hyperspawn mechanic not apply?

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/014 - I Finally Unlocked WESTFALL, Time To Farm! - Goldbound Episode 14.en-orig.txt
source.quote: But unfortunately, just like a couple minutes into this farm, the drop rates are feeling terrible. We're only getting one or two linen cloth every 10 to 15 NLES. So, my best guess is that Blizzard actually patched this farm and the drop rates were tanked to avoid the fiveman farms from flooding the market. Oh well. And if you watched the Elwin episodes, you might be asking, why do we even care about linen cloth? Wasn't it noted that it wasn't even profitable beyond shirt crafting? Well, you might also remember we were close to testing a tailoring and enchanting shuffle. The only missing piece was the reagents for the relics of the past, which allow you to scale low-level greens up in item level, which may allow us to disenchant greens crafted from linen cloth for higher mats or more mats, all from just linen. And until now, couldn't make relics of the past or obtain them from any zone vendors. But while I was exploring Westfall, looking for maybe new profession trainers, which unfortunately there's no new profession trainers, I did come across a trade good vendor in the inn. And guess what? He not only sells the reagent we need to craft the relics from the past, but he just straight up sells the relics themselves.

source.cleaned_file: goldbound/014 - I Finally Unlocked WESTFALL, Time To Farm! - Goldbound Episode 14.en-orig.txt
source.quote: Dungeons. So, let's go back into Deadmines and test the cloth rates. Now, it's pretty apparent after a few Deadmines runs that bag space again is a massive limitation for our account right now. We do have four travelers backpacks, which are 16 slot bags, which are the highest bags we can get from drops in classic zones, but we can only do about two runs of dead mines before they fill up fully. And we have to do some inventory management. That forces us to hearth back to Goldshshire to vendor off at the inn and then fly north to Stormwind to bank the transmog and trade goods and then finally fly back to Moonbrook. Now that full cycle is about 20 minutes for two runs. So at best we hit about six runs per hour. Now on a druid with larger bags, you could hit the 10 run lockout in about 40 minutes. But hey, this is gold bound and we make do. And after an hour, so six full runs, we actually pulled in 783 linen cloth, which is easily our best cloth farm so far. And we can farm it endlessly without the drop rates going down. On top of that, Ludapra actually clocked in 583 raw gold from the dungeon. And this is just looted gold, which doesn't include vendor, which is rare for us cuz most of our gold comes in the mailbox. So, we might want to keep a bit more of attention to the actual gold in the inventory through each episode now. And with the clock stacking up, it's time travelers. We're going to drop mining and herbalism, which we leveled up to 300 in Swamposauros, and grab tailoring and enchanting to test the new shuffle. And for context, linen cloth only sells for about 17 silver each. So, our 783 cloth is not worth a fortune as is. But with the shuffle, maybe we can squeeze some more value out of it. And here's the plan. So, at level 30 tailoring, we can craft green level gloves and pants. Each of these are the prime shuffle crafts because they only require two bolts of linen cloth, which is four linen cloth total once you've made the bolts, which means these are the cheapest green quality disenchantable linen gear you can make. And our new friend sells relics of the past ranks one through six, which each scale the item to a higher level all the way up to 350.

source.quote: strange dust 80% of the time and lesser magic essences 20% of the time. So, the relics do actually improve the enchanting, but the scaling levels don't. So, stick to rank one, the cheapest ones we can get. So, to test this properly for base craft versus rank one craft, I crafted up 100 rank one gloves and disenchant them. Now, this only took 10 minutes and actually yielded a total of 604 gold, including 38 greater eternal essences. That averages to just over six gold per craft. And so even after subtracting the relic cost, that's a net profit of about four gold 73 silver per craft, which effectively means every linen cloth is worth over one gold since each craft is four linen cloth, which isn't insane, but it's reliable, especially since we'll be farming dead mines routinely anyways. And for comparison, I also disenchanted 50 base rank, but netted only 151 gold, or about three gold per craft, meaning the relics actually increased the profit per craft by one gold, 70 silver, at least from a disenchanting angle. So, this works, and it's a real improvement on our cloth farms, and finally makes linen cloth farming and dead mines a viable gold source. I'm glad we finally came full circle on relics. But okay, travelers, with that out of the way, it's time to head back out there for some farming.

source.quote: But this time, I have an idea that might actually fight off the open world loot bugs. I mean, sorry, anti-hyperspawn mechanics. And to test it, we're headed to the coast. And no, we're not fishing. Well, not yet, at least. We're going murloc hunting. Now, the shoreline here is packed with all kinds of murlocs and all kinds of crabs. And a few of them carry some very specific drops worth chasing. And my thought is, if we just move steadily from the northern shore all the way down to the southern shore, killing everything along the way, maybe we can trick the game's anti-hyperspawn code. As far as the loot tables will be concerned, we'll just be one lone adventurer questing along the beach. I mean, it's worth a test. So, let's update the macro for Murlocs and look at the loot tables. So, first off, there's about eight or nine different kinds of murlocs, but there's a few we want to look out for. The murloc warriors. These spawn mostly in the center coast, but can drop the driftwood club. And this club goes for 3,000 on North American servers and 83,000 on European servers.

source.quote: These are found a little more southern on the shore and they can drop the foam spittle staff which is basically Westfall's version of the Riverside staff. And these things are valued at 30 to 40,000 gold. And they do have a low posted drop rate as well, but I think they may have been unavailable for some time which artificially lowers the recorded drop rate on Wowhead. But either way, we'll be farming it. And then there's the sea crawlers. These guys are in the middle of the coast and they drop the long crawler limb, which is a transmog weapon valued at around 2.7 to 5,000 gold. Even just a couple of these sales would be a long way towards unlocking our next token because right now we're only at 5,000 gold. And so running the entire coast on a rogue took me about 13 to 16 minutes tagging all of the murlocs and crawlers on the coast.

source.quote: Now, this of course is not as fast as a druid speed set farmer, but it's still a ton of kills. Now, so far, I haven't pulled any crazy drops, but a few whites and a few greens, and I'll for sure keep farming this route to Stalker Auctionos. And on this one, we do take out all of the Merlocs and crawlers, not just the ones I've named here, because they do all have decent world drop loot tables. And anecdotally, my current measuring stick for whether the anti-hyperspawn mechanic is active is simple. If we stop seeing cloth drop, probably means it's in effect. But we're seeing cloth dropping consistently across the whole shore over a 15-minute farm session, which means I think our method actually getting a round of the anti-hyperspawn mechanic. Now, it is worth noting that this route does actually overlap with a few of Westfall's rares. Now, Westfall does have quite a few rares, but the two in our way here are murlocs right on the coast. First, there's Slark, who spawns on the Northshore, and he seems to have a pretty quick respawn time of 15 to 20 minutes, which kind of lines up perfectly with this actual route. And his big drop is the Coral Claymore, a clean emerald tinge sword valued at around 20 to 40,000 gold and definitely one of our zone targets. Then there's Brack. He's found on the more southern shore and he also drops Brack Claw, a simple dagger which has a value of around 15 to 30,000 gold. While we're running our coastline strat, we'll try to tag Slark and Brack whenever we can just to increase our total loot value.

source.file: 014 - I Finally Unlocked WESTFALL, Time To Farm! - Goldbound Episode 14.en-orig.vtt
source.cleaned_file: goldbound/014 - I Finally Unlocked WESTFALL, Time To Farm! - Goldbound Episode 14.en-orig.txt
source.quote: But travelers, while I was working on this coastal farm, I actually discovered another one. Now, I had planned to do the small egg farm here in Westfall since there's flesh rippers roaming the zone all over the place. And we already know that those eggs are used as a currency during the Feast of Winter's Veil event, which is only 6 weeks away now. So, prices are sure to climb as we get closer. And originally, I thought the Flesh Rippers were too spread out across the mainland to make for a strong farm. But it's not quite the case. About halfway up the shore near this small inlet, there is what looks to be a massive beached fish. Maybe one of Nat Pegle's legendary catches that he couldn't quite drag home. But around this fish, exactly three fleshers. And guess what? They're on a mini hyperspawn. Now, most hyperspawns require five to 30 mobs and multiple players holding positions down to keep the cycle going. But these guys, if we stand off just to one side of the fish, even our 30-yard pistol shot can range all three birds without moving. Which means we can literally stand in one spot, press one key, and endlessly farm flesh rippers. Now, the anti-hyperspawn mechanic still applies to most items, greens and trade goods and all that, but for some reason, small eggs aren't affected. So, as long as the flesh rippers keep spawning, they keep dropping the eggs at roughly a 65% drop chance. As long as they keep spawning is a key point here. This doesn't seem to be a true infinite hyperspawn.

source.quote: After about 10 to 20 minutes, they tend to slow down quite a bit and the spawn rates dip. But even after only 27 minutes of testing, I ended up with 194 small eggs. At a current market price of 9 gold, 51 silver, that's 1,844 gold. from just under half an hour of farming. And with most of our Westfall farms so far being transmog, this might become a staple, especially if small eggs prices spike closer to Winter's Veil. Of course, since we can't farm this one indefinitely, we have to let it reset for the spawn rates to go back up. We'll need something to fill in the gaps between respawn cycles. And I have just the thing. It's time to go fishing, travelers. And you might think, we're already on the coast, so are we doing coastal fishing or pool fishing? Well, not yet, because Westfall has one of the coolest ultra RNG fishing farms, in my opinion, in the entire game. Now, in the middle of the zone, there's a small, unassuming lake. Well, more of a pond.

source.quote: And most of the fish here are standard, the same as Elwin, maybe 20 to 30 gold per hour. Really nothing to write home about. Although, I did fish up some Buccaneers gear while testing this. And we actually got our first Stendull Bane. So, we can go ahead and open this up and see if we got the jackpot. Well, no ring this time. Better luck next time, I suppose. All right, but we've had a pretty full week here in Westfall with a heavy focus on Dead Mines, transmog farming, and disenchanting. So, let's head back to the bank and go over the loot we've stockpiled from Deadmines so far. And I held it all in the bank without posting on the auction house just to give a better view of what we've actually gotten from this dungeon that's notable.

Otherwise, mostly smaller sales this time around. And with only about 6 days since the last mailbox opening, we're just at 105 total males. So, let's get these all collected and see how we did. All right. So, not the biggest mailbox clear. Um, and I'll also go ahead and hop over to Stormwind to grab our transmog sales because, well, it wasn't much better. Only 1,500 gold and no notable items. Now, I knew this might happen. Spending so much time farming dead mines and holding all the loot in the bank to show it off definitely slowed things down because they weren't listed until this video was done, but it's all listed now and we'll see what moves next week. That said, we need to start making some serious progress if we're going to earn another WoW token anytime soon.

source.quote: And then a few journeyman staves and buccaneer set pieces, but all of them are pretty much under 2,000 gold here. Now, on to the blues. And this is where we kind of called our shots with what was actually dropping. And we pulled three Defias Rapiers. Now, these do have a good appearance. I was debating equipping them for our current zone transmog, but personally, I'm still partial to the the Blackwater Cutless and the Buzzerblade Transmog combo. We also did get one goblin screwdriver, a stonemason cloak, and even a pair of blackened Defas leggings from the Defas Overseers. We also got a few of the woodworking and metalworking gloves, too. Now, all in all, DeadMines's transmog kind of caps out around 4k per piece. But if a few of these sell, it could make a noticeable dent in the transmog. It could make a good dent in our next token price. And travelers, after all that farming, crafting, and disenchanting, and I mean a lot of disenchanting, it's time to check out our new mailbox. So, let's see what Westfall has brought us this week. Let's not waste any time and get straight into the mailbox. And as expected, we do have a bunch of illusion dust going and other enchanting materials moving as well.
